chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: Why he left Norvo for Goodman
summary: He took Goodman's salary to pay for lessons, after asking Red to pay him to write rather than play.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Before we go any further with that, why don't we go back a step and talk about when you left Red and went with Benny.
Why did I do it? I often wondered that myself.
Do you regret having done it?

No, because I think my real reason for going with Benny was to get enough money so that I could pay these teachers. I was putting out about thirty, thirty five dollars a week for lessons in those days.
That's steep even now.
Even now?
Yes.
This was for two lessons a week, not for one. I went twice a week.
I couldn't do it, Red was too sporadic and Benny at least gave me the possibility of it being somewhat steady.
You were on salary?
Yes.
With Red too I got whatever the guys got. If they got sixty dollars a week that's what I'd get. Mostly it was like that.

What was that story I read in that interview you did with Michael Brooks, that you were playing trumpet in section and you just went to Red one day and said, do I have to play trumpet, why can't you just pay me equivalent to what one of the guys would make and just let me write.
That's probably true. I think I probably did that. That was in Chicago and that's the way it went.
Red didn't have any money; what could he do?
Yeah, really.
I was aware of that
and I didn't need much, but then I did get married and I wanted money; that was the other reason.

Also, I suppose a touch of ambition at that point. I don't know what I wanted but I wanted something more, and that's what drove me to take those lessons and I realized later that one of the reasons was to keep my mind working in an area that it wasn't given in a normal, daily routine. It was always something beyond what I encountered it would be, the type of thinking, a speculative way of looking at things.
The carry over of that into the daily work that I did might have countered for my not being accepted commercially, which I was not. I was put down very early on for being too wild.
